name: Beechcraft Musketeer / Sundowner / Sierra
variants: Model 23 / A23 / B23 / C23 Musketeer & Sundowner (160–180 hp)
summary: Four-seat all-metal low-wing from Beechcraft built 1963–83, known for a wide cabin and sturdy fixed gear; the Sierra variant has retractable landing gear.

wings: Wing mounted low on a deep, wide fuselage
engines: Single flat-four in a smooth, rounded cowling
fuselage: Wide four-seat cabin with large side windows
Fixed tricycle gear with short, stout legs and pants (retractable on the Sierra)
tail: Tall, swept fin with a rounded top

tellTales: Low wing, wide cabin and tall swept fin on fixed tricycle gear
Rounded cowling on a stocky fuselage with a low-set horizontal tail

confusedWith.howToTell: The Musketeer has a rounder, wider cabin and a taller, more swept fin; the PA-28 has a narrower cabin, an all-flying stabilator and a lower, squarer fin.
The Musketeer has a low-set horizontal tail and four seats; the Skipper is a smaller two-seater with a T-tail.
The Musketeer is a low-wing with no struts; the 172 is a high-wing braced by a strut each side.
The Musketeer has a conventional hinged-cabin four-seat layout with a swept fin; the AA-5 has a sliding bubble canopy and a shorter, rounder fuselage.
